name: Akhetaten / Amarna
summary: A long, unwalled riverside city in a desert bay: open-air temple courts, elite compounds, small houses, irrigated plots and cliffs.

features.label: City massing & scale
features.text: Schematic urban ribbon, not a measured whole-city polygon; river and cliff spacing is interpretive. Roof count, household arrangement, wall trace and building heights are visual modeling choices.

features.label: Roads, tracks & paths
features.text: Feature types and broad connections may be documented; all rendered centerlines are interpretive, not surveyed ancient itineraries. Routes are drawn as earth surfaces, without modern asphalt or road signage.

features.label: Vegetation & cultivation
features.text: Regional and selected site evidence informs the palette. Canopy cover, exact species placements, field boundaries, season and animal counts are illustrative. Forest coverage is not quantified; no modern forest-cover layer is backdated. This pass separates orchards, riparian growth and open woodland; visible patch densities remain illustrative. The supplied report is a regional synthesis, not a new local excavation.

features.label: Water & landform
features.text: Original analytic terrain shaped to broad documented landform character. Not a DEM, historical elevation survey, or recovered ancient shoreline. Rivers, shorelines and canal layouts are study geometry and cannot be used as geographic survey coordinates.

features.label: Animal life
features.text: Small sheep/goat/cattle herds and bird silhouettes provide scale and life. Movements, counts and locations are not historical observations. Wildlife is not presented as a complete species inventory. The new landscape report does not provide a comprehensive dated fauna inventory, so no new wildlife species are inferred from its vegetation records.

features.label: Regional ecology · supplied report
features.text: River-supported fields, marshes, levees and wooded margins contrast with desert. Adaïma charcoal supports a local early wooded-margin interpretation, not an Egypt-wide closed forest. The Delta, Giza, Luxor and Middle Egypt have different records. At Luxor a wandering/braided river preceded less-dynamic straight/anabranching channels; the modern single-thread local planform postdates the atlas interval. Limits: Do not transfer the Luxor core history directly to Amarna. Exact branch positions and Egypt-wide forest percentages are not supplied. Sediment dates are approximate. Source: supplied report, pages 2, 3.
